About Me

Learning scientist.
Instructional designer.
EdTech evaluator.

"Good learning design isn't about the technology. It's about what happens in the learner's mind."

I'm a learning scientist and instructional designer with a PhD in Educational Technology from IIT Bombay, where I was awarded India's prestigious Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (top 0.5% of applicants).

My work lives at the intersection of learning science, assessment design, and educational technology. I've built interactive learning environments that help bioscience students develop clinical reasoning skills, designed frameworks that guide how governments invest in EdTech, and created open educational resources used by college teachers across India.

I bring both the rigour of a researcher — mixed methods, learning analytics, rubric validation — and the craft of a designer who has shipped real products used by real learners.

Technology-Enhanced Learning Environment

Karyotype

Interactive case-based learning for clinical diagnosis of genetic disorders

The Problem
Undergraduate bioscience students struggle to develop clinical reasoning skills in genetics — the gap between textbook knowledge and real diagnostic thinking.
What I Built
Designed end-to-end — pedagogy, UI/UX, interactive elements (H5P + Genially), assessment rubrics, patient case narratives, and learning activity sequences. Ran workshops validating the design with learners and instructors.
📌 Case-based Learning 🧬 Bioscience Education 📐 End-to-end Design 🔬 Mixed Methods Research

Open Educational Resource

JeevAdhyayan / CTRL-B

OER repository for biology teachers — made by teachers, for teachers

What I Built
Designed the full repository structure, template system, and curation framework. CTRL-B enables college teachers to create and share inquiry-based, case-driven learning resources using predict-observe-explain pedagogy.
🌿 Inquiry-based 📚 OER Design 🔗 Extension of Karyotype

Research

Selected Publications

View All on Google Scholar ↗
2024 · Peer-reviewed Journal

"Professional Identity Development in Bioscience Education: A Systematic Review"

Educational Research and Reviews (ERR)

A comprehensive systematic review of how undergraduate science students develop professional identity — synthesising evidence on what instructional approaches support this development.

Read Paper →
2024 · International Conference

"Making Sense of Students' Sensemaking in Karyotype: A TELE for Clinical Diagnosis"

31st International Conference on Learning (ICL)

Empirical study showing how learners construct clinical reasoning in Karyotype — tracking cognitive and affective dimensions of sensemaking through case-based inquiry tasks.

Read Paper →
2023 · IEEE ICALT

"Students' Involvement in a Sensemaking Task and Its Effect on Self-Efficacy"

IEEE International Conference on Advanced Learning Technologies

Demonstrates how engaging students in authentic sensemaking tasks improves self-efficacy — with implications for designing assessments that build learner confidence alongside competence.

Read Paper →
